clue.text: Bounder took female in — obtained money

indicators.note: 'took ... in' says the female pronoun is taken inside the word for the bounder

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, an old word for a dishonourable man
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A scoundrel took a woman in, and pocketed the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash a cheque is to turn it into money, so cashed means obtained money for it.

parts.note: to cap is to complete or top off

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A rebellion on an island, carried out with total skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means skilled and competent, a synonym of accomplished.

clue.text: It might be the last straw for loyal supporters

indicators.note: 'It might be' says the following words might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Devoted backers finally losing patience, the last straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwarts are dependable, steadfast adherents of a cause or team.

clue.text: Rex seen around about low part of Devon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the cattle sound
'seen around' tells us the king's name is turned about into a new order

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex spotted wandering a lowland patch of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' scrambles the king's name to EXR, and 'about' wraps that round the cow's sound. Devon is a county in south-west England, and 'Rex' looks like a dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This moorland national park lies largely in Somerset and partly in Devon.

parts.note: to bar something is to forbid or not allow it
gains are profits

explanation.surface: A rule that cut-price goods may not earn their sellers any profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargains are goods bought cheaply, a common synonym for cut-price items.

clue.text: A Blue, not with university, showing talent

indicators.note: 'not with' means the university letter is removed

parts.note: taken as the colour word itself

explanation.surface: A sportsman who earned his Blue without going to university, a real talent.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLUE is a sporting award at Oxford or Cambridge, which makes the university link in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilful, possessing talent.

parts.note: gains means wins
aid means support or help

explanation.surface: A candidate wins backing even when facing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsaid is the past tense of a formal verb meaning denied or contradicted.

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A discreet hotel used by the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private, personal, not shown outwardly.

clue.text: She is given two articles in a case

parts.note: taken as written
the indefinite and definite articles, a and the
the indefinite and definite articles, a and the

explanation.surface: A woman is handed two pieces of luggage packed in a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put a blade into its scabbard, which is a case for it.

clue.text: Job is finished, and these songs start

definitions.text: Job is finished, and these songs start

parts.words: Job is finished, and these songs start
parts.note: in the Old Testament the Book of Job is followed immediately by the book of sacred songs attributed to David

explanation.surface: A worker downs tools and the singing begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like a task, but it is the biblical book; once it ends, the next book of the Bible begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The book after Job is a collection of 150 sacred songs or hymns, the biblical songbook.

indicators.note: the daughter abandoning the word means her letter leaves it

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual flirtation or romance

explanation.surface: A daughter gives up a fling in favour of a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance can be a union by marriage, especially between families or dynasties.

parts.note: 'Relatively' looks like 'comparatively' but means favourable towards one's relatives

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly'; read as 'to relatives', it describes favouritism in families.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes favouritism shown to family members in giving jobs or posts.

definitions.meaning: to astonish or overwhelm someone, an idiom meaning to stun
someone who loves the bow, the archer's weapon, read as a two-word phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to astonish; read literally it is a fan of the bow, as an archer might be.

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so the letters of the clergyman's title are set in motion

explanation.surface: A lively clergyman shows a sharp sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for liveliness of mind and quick wit.

clue.text: Uniformly gusty with initial change of direction

indicators.note: the first letter, a compass point, changes to another compass point

parts.note: squally means gusty, windy

explanation.surface: Windy weather that suddenly shifts direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial change of direction' swaps the opening S (south) for E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: Equally means in the same way or to the same degree, uniformly.

clue.text: Book the last waltz in time

indicators.note: the picked letter is placed in the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: 'the last' picks the final letter of the word waltz

explanation.surface: A dance-hall evening ending with the final waltz, played in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, named after the scribe.

clue.text: Assume ten love being held by rather a chivalrous character

parts.note: to don is to put on or assume clothing or a role

indicators.note: the ten and love are held inside the word for rather

parts.note: quite means rather, fairly
X is the Roman numeral for ten
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Assume a ten-love lead is held, rather like a gallant knight would.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's deluded knight-errant is the archetype of idealistic, impractical gallantry.

clue.text: Be more than an issue after being made public

indicators.note: the issue comes after the word for made public

parts.note: out means revealed, made public
a number is an issue of a magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine sells beyond expectation after its release.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber is to exceed in quantity, to be more than another group.

indicators.note: a creation is something made anew, so the letters are formed into something different

explanation.surface: An Italian invention credited to the radio pioneer Marconi.
explanation.definitionFit: This tube-shaped pasta is a classic product of Italian cuisine.

parts.note: a native of one particular Central American republic, between Nicaragua and Panama, which is a Latin American person

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition; the answer is simply one kind of Latin American, so the solver must find the nationality from the enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of that Central American country is one example of a Latin American.

clue.text: Makes a fuss when a secret is found out

indicators.note: found out suggests the letters are dug out and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss when a secret is uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal usage, to create means to make a fuss or complain loudly.

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; read as plural, favourites are pets

explanation.surface: A star's support behind the scenes of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favourite's' is read as a plural, pets, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, a synonym in the sense of a phase.

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Halting something before it begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening.

indicators.note: the site includes the letter a inside it

parts.note: a place is a site or location

explanation.surface: A location featuring a magnificent home.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, especially of a monarch.

clue.text: They won't top the bill, in any form

definitions.text: They won't top the bill, in any form

parts.words: They won't top the bill, in any form
parts.note: film background performers never get star billing, in any production

explanation.walkthrough: 'top the bill' suggests a price, but it is the list of performers; 'form' may also hint at a fee for anything added.
explanation.definitionFit: Background actors in films are never named at the top of the cast list.

clue.text: Claw used in fight along with teeth

indicators.note: 'used in' says the letters are contained within the words fight along

explanation.surface: An animal fighting with claws and teeth together.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

indicators.note: the meadows are seen inside the word for unspoilt

parts.note: pure means unspoilt
leas are meadows, a poetic word for grassland

explanation.surface: Fields that are untouched by man are a joy to behold.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a synonym for delight or enjoyment.

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A politician framed in a news broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn means stitched together, joined with needle and thread.

definitions.meaning: to debate a matter at length
the time when talks are ended, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means debate thoroughly; read literally it is the moment the talk is done.

parts.note: 'pretty' looks like an adverb meaning fairly, but it is an adjective: a showy trinket of no use

explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty useless' reads as 'rather useless'; the setter means an object that is pretty but useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A bauble is a showy trinket or decoration with little practical value.

clue.text: Aware ten is ten? Could be!

indicators.note: 'Could be!' suggests the letters could be reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether ten equals ten, with a shrugging reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and feel, conscious, hence aware.

definitions.meaning: a small domesticated polecat used for catching rabbits
to search about persistently, as in rummaging

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the weasel-like creature; the verb means to search for something persistently.
